examples.description: Assert that a billing client IS an on-platform business

failure_modes.recovery: Ask them to grant it (Network → Consent), then retry. Do exactly what this error says — there is no workaround lane.
failure_modes.when: the counterparty business has not granted 'cross_tenant_settlement' consent (or its grant's claims exclude link_tenant)

failure_modes.recovery: Links ride real relationships: match or open a deal thread first (network tools), then link.
failure_modes.when: no network relationship (active match or deal thread) exists with that business, or the client id is not yours

failure_modes.recovery: A client cannot be linked to your own tenant — pass the OTHER business's tenant id, or null to unlink.
failure_modes.when: counterparty_tenant_id names your own tenant, or a required argument is missing

preconditions: The counterparty must have granted 'cross_tenant_settlement' consent AND share a network relationship (active match or deal thread) with you.
Pass counterparty_tenant_id null to UNLINK — the same approval-gated door; history stays in the event trail.
The client's existing invoices are retro-stamped in the same call (invoices_stamped in the result is the count) — read it back with invoice_client_read before you report done.

description: [REQUIRES APPROVAL] Asserts that a billing client IS an on-platform tenant (or pass counterparty_tenant_id null to unlink) and retro-stamps that client's existing invoices with the link in the same call — invoices_stamped in the result is the count. Linking requires the counterparty's 'cross_tenant_settlement' consent AND a live network relationship (an active match or a deal thread); unlinking passes neither gate, since it withdraws your own assertion rather than making a new one. NEXT: invoice_client_read to read back what linked.

counterparty_tenant_id.description: The on-platform business this client IS (their tenant id). Pass null to unlink.

name: invoice_client_link_tenant
